clauses.reason: The order approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Commercial and Breeder Hatchery Industry under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act: it directs that "do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Commercial and Breeder Hatchery Industry". The approval follows findings that the code complies with section 3(a) of Title I. The command has no operative effect apart from section 3 of Title I. Under section 3 of Title I an approved code supplied the standards of fair competition, equity enforcement by the district courts and criminal liability for violations; the repeal of the provisions providing for enforcement of codes removed those effects prospectively. Section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113, approved on the date stated in the resolution as "Approved, June 14, 1935.", provides that all the provisions of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes "are hereby repealed"; the resolution states no other effective date for section 2. The approval therefore ceased to operate on June 14, 1935. A. L. A. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, decided May 27, 1935, is recorded as a validity characterization (the section 3 code-making delegation was held unconstitutional; under the doctrine then prevailing an approval made under it was void from issuance), not as an end date, because no held record shows that the government cancelled or suspended this code on that date. June 16, 1935, the original two-year expiry of Title I, is not an end: section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with "on April 1, 1936".

inventory_overrides.reason: The numbered items 1 to 5 are findings that are the statutory predicate for approval, not commands; the only operative command is the closing approval sentence, which is the corrected inventory.

research_rationale:
Executive order approving the Code of Fair Competition for the Commercial and Breeder Hatchery Industry under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. Applying the reviewed shared analysis: the code-dependent command had no own-terms end, no held record shows an earlier cancellation or suspension, and Senate Joint Resolution 113 section 2 (June 14, 1935) repealed the code approval and enforcement provisions, so the approval ended on June 14, 1935. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date. The machine inventory treated the five numbered findings as five operative clauses; they are the statutory findings that the application was made, notice and hearings were given, the code complies with section 3(a)(1) and (2) and will tend to effectuate the policy of Title I, and the only command is the final approval, to which the inventory is corrected. The order cites only Title I of NIRA, not the Agricultural Adjustment Act. The text is an American Presidency Project transcription held as a provisional working text under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling; no certification is claimed.

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the Code of Fair Competition for the Commercial and Breeder Hatchery Industry before June 14, 1935, and any fine, injunction or conviction already completed, are accrued effects that the repeal did not undo; the section 5 antitrust exemption for action already taken under an approved and effective code is likewise an accrued effect. The proviso to section 2 of the resolution names agreements and action thereunder and states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed that exemption for past action under codes. No held source continues the approval after June 14, 1935 and no held source shows a prosecution under this code continued after that date; nothing here continues the approval itself.

source_notes.reason: A. L. A. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States judgment: the section 3 code-making delegation was held unconstitutional and the code provisions in question invalid; recorded as the validity characterization that applies to every section 3 approval, not as an end of this order.
